plain_text:
Researching and developing new treatments for
rare diseases is time consuming, complex, and
often expensive. Most rare diseases (almost 80%)
are caused by a defect in a single gene. Because of this, gene
therapies - treatments where certain genes are adjusted to
treat someone's disease - are a promising approach for
some diseases. These treatments "fix" the genetic mutations
(harmful changes) that cause some diseases by replacing or
changing a gene that doesn't work with one that does.
semantic_text: Researching and developing new treatments for rare diseases is time consuming, complex, and often expensive. Most rare diseases (almost 80%) are caused by a defect in a single gene. Because of this, gene therapies - treatments where certain genes are adjusted to treat someone's disease - are a promising approach for some diseases. These treatments "fix" the genetic mutations (harmful changes) that cause some diseases by replacing or changing a gene that doesn't work with one that does.

plain_text:
Because specific rare diseases generally only affect a few
hundred people, pharmaceutical companies aren't usually
interested in developing treatments for them.
semantic_text: Because specific rare diseases generally only affect a few hundred people, pharmaceutical companies aren't usually interested in developing treatments for them.

plain_text:
That's where NIH research comes in. This article
describes two rare diseases – spinal muscular atrophy and
Duchenne muscular dystrophy – and how NIH supports
research and development on gene therapies to treat them.
semantic_text: That's where NIH research comes in. This article describes two rare diseases – spinal muscular atrophy and Duchenne muscular dystrophy – and how NIH supports research and development on gene therapies to treat them.

plain_text:
A medication called nusinersen was one of the first genetic
therapies approved for a rare disease. It treats a group of rare
genetic disorders called spinal muscular atrophies (SMAs)
that cause loss of nerve cells that control skeletal muscles
(muscles that allow us to move) leading to weakness.
semantic_text: A medication called nusinersen was one of the first genetic therapies approved for a rare disease. It treats a group of rare genetic disorders called spinal muscular atrophies (SMAs) that cause loss of nerve cells that control skeletal muscles (muscles that allow us to move) leading to weakness.

plain_text:
SMAs start in infancy or early childhood and are a leading
cause of death in infants and toddlers. There are a few
different SMAs, and all of them are caused by a mutation
in a gene called SMN1 (which stands for “survival motor
neuron”). SMN1 helps the body make an important protein
that keeps the nerves that control muscle movement
healthy. Because people with SMAs don’t make enough
SMN proteins, some of their muscles (like the ones that
help us move, breathe, and swallow), don’t work correctly.
In the most severe cases, this can cause paralysis and death.
There’s no cure for SMA, but there are treatments to help
prevent and manage its symptoms.

There are a few different SMAs, and all of them are caused by a mutation in a gene called SMN1 (which stands for “survival motor neuron”). SMN1 helps the body make an important protein that keeps the nerves that control muscle movement healthy. Because people with SMAs don’t make enough SMN proteins, some of their muscles (like the ones that help us move, breathe, and swallow), don’t work correctly. In the most severe cases, this can cause paralysis and death. There’s no cure for SMA, but there are treatments to help prevent and manage its symptoms.

plain_text:
In some rare diseases, DNA mutations cause a gene
or protein to work incorrectly. The National Institute of
Neurological Disorders and Stroke (NINDS) supports
research and development on therapies that work at the
genetic level to “fix” those problems in children and adults
with SMA.
semantic_text: In some rare diseases, DNA mutations cause a gene or protein to work incorrectly. The National Institute of Neurological Disorders and Stroke (NINDS) supports research and development on therapies that work at the genetic level to “fix” those problems in children and adults with SMA.

plain_text:
Nusinersen targets another gene called SMN2 that also
makes a small amount of the SMN protein. It helps muscles
and nerves work properly by changing the SMN2 gene product
to make more of the SMN protein than it usually would.
semantic_text: Nusinersen targets another gene called SMN2 that also makes a small amount of the SMN protein. It helps muscles and nerves work properly by changing the SMN2 gene product to make more of the SMN protein than it usually would.

plain_text:
There's another gene-based therapy for children under
age 2 that uses a safe virus to deliver a new copy of the SMN
gene into specific neurons to improve muscle movement.
semantic_text: There's another gene-based therapy for children under age 2 that uses a safe virus to deliver a new copy of the SMN gene into specific neurons to improve muscle movement.

plain_text:
There are about 7,000 known
rare diseases, but only
a few have treatments
approved by the Food and Drug
Administration.
semantic_text: There are about 7,000 known rare diseases, but only a few have treatments approved by the Food and Drug Administration.
